title: Persistent Mean Tracking in Client--Server Open Networks
summary: We study persistent-agent identification and mean tracking in an open client-server network where agents participate intermittently. The network consists of a core of highly regular persistent agents and a subset of transient/non-persistent agents that appear only sporadically. Since the server observes only binary activity indicators and scalar updates from active agents, naive averaging cannot recover the active persistent mean because transient-agent updates contaminate the aggregate, and heterogeneous participation introduces bias.
